exposure: Intrathecal Nalbuphine (0.7 mg) with 0.5% bupivacaine (10 mg)
Intrathecal Magnesium Sulphate (25 mg) with 0.5% bupivacaine (10 mg)
outcome: Time to reach sensory level of T5
Motor block onset (time to reach MBS-3)
Time to regress motor blockade to MBS-1
cohort: 70 parturients between the ages of 20-40 years undergoing lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Both intrathecal nalbuphine and magnesium sulphate with bupivacaine are safe and effective in reducing the frequency and severity of shivering during LSCS under spinal anaesthesia without causing serious side effects.
